data.title: Bitcoin Doesn't Need a Bank, yet Strategy Wants to Become One
data.description: Strategy wants to become the world’s Bitcoin bank, with Michael Saylor reiterating the goal on November 6, 2026. According to BeInCrypto, CEO Phong Le outlined the plan at Money20/20, describing the company’s evolution into a holder of 845,000 BTC. Separately, an on-chain researcher said Bitcoin’s blockchain reached 780 GB in 2026, small enough to fit on a 1TB drive and allow users to run a full node.

data.title: Crypto Liquidations Total $72.64M in 24 Hours, Including $48.23M in Longs and $24.41M in Shorts
data.description: According to ChainCatcher citing Coinglass, crypto liquidations totaled $72.64 million over the past 24 hours, with $48.23 million in long positions and $24.41 million in short positions liquidated. Bitcoin accounted for $4.661 million in long liquidations and $3.938 million in short liquidations, while Ethereum saw $4.538 million in long liquidations and $4.216 million in short liquidations.

data.title: Paraguay's Former President Faces Prosecutors After Removal Over Ueno Bank Collapse
data.description: According to CNBC, former Paraguayan President Santiago Peña was questioned by prosecutors Saturday after Congress removed him over the collapse of Ueno Bank. Prosecutors had ordered the arrest of Peña and former Central Bank chief Carlos Carvallo on Friday as part of a criminal investigation into alleged breach of trust and other offenses. Regulators seized Ueno Bank three days before Peña's removal, freezing access to savings for nearly 3 million customers. The Central Bank said Saturday that 1.2 million customers had received partial or full reimbursement of insured deposits.

data.title: Former FBI Agent Admits Stealing $2.47 Million in Cryptocurrency, Faces Up to 20 Years in Prison
data.description:
Former FBI agent Patrick Steven Yaroch admitted stealing about $2.47 million in cryptocurrency and pleaded guilty to wire fraud and money laundering on November 5. According to Foresight News, the U.S. Department of Justice said Yaroch used credentials obtained through his position to make about 100 fraudulent transfers involving 35 separate investigations.

The stolen assets came from wallets controlled by investigation subjects and hostile state actors, as well as at least one wallet the FBI created for an operation. Court documents say Yaroch concealed the funds’ origins through asset conversions and repeated transfers, and used some of the money to pay personal debts. The Justice Department said his conduct damaged investigations and related intelligence sources and methods. Sentencing is scheduled for March 4, 2027, and Yaroch faces up to 20 years in prison.

data.title: AI | Ken Chenault Urges Executives to Uphold Values Amid AI Pressures
data.description: General Catalyst Chairman and Managing Director and former American Express CEO Ken Chenault said executives need the courage to stand by their values as political and technological pressures intensify, Bloomberg reported. Speaking with host David Gura on Bloomberg This Weekend, Chenault said companies should pursue innovation while protecting safety, broadening opportunity and ensuring AI improves people's lives.

data.title: Kevin O’Leary Says His Michael Jordan Card Is Worth $2 Million
data.description: Kevin O’Leary says his 1997-98 Fleer Metal Universe Precious Metal Gems Red Michael Jordan card is worth more than $2 million; his investment group reportedly paid between $500,000 and $600,000. The valuation has not been confirmed by a public auction, according to BeInCrypto; another Jordan PMG Red sold for $1,473,989 in August 2026. O’Leary owns card No. 12 of 100 and wants 5% of his portfolio in sports cards. A rare Pokémon-card index gained more than 150% between September 2021 and October 2026, but collectibles generate no income, can take time to sell and depend on buyer demand.

data.title: Missy Mazzoli Is First Woman Composer With a Metropolitan Opera World Premiere
data.description: Composer Missy Mazzoli discussed adapting George Saunders’s “Lincoln in the Bardo” for the Metropolitan Opera, where she became the first woman composer to have a world premiere, according to Bloomberg. On Bloomberg This Weekend, she told hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini that punk shaped her musical sensibility and that her long collaboration with librettist Royce Vavrek was essential to turning Saunders’s ghost story into an opera.

data.title: Protein Demand Drives Billions in Livestock Health Investment
data.description: Animal health companies are investing billions of dollars to expand businesses focused on improving the health of cattle, pigs and poultry for human consumption, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: Vitalik Buterin Says SHIB Donation Worth Hundreds of Millions Exceeded His Expectations
data.description: According to ChainCatcher, Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin said in an October 29 interview on the Silicon Valley 101 podcast that he did not expect his SHIB donation to be worth hundreds of millions of dollars and would have made a different decision had he known. He recalled investing $25,000 in DOGE, which later grew in value to more than $10 million. The SHIB project had sent half of its total token supply to his public wallet. Buterin sold some of the tokens for about $70 million in ETH but held a large remainder because of limited market liquidity, then donated it to an Indian COVID relief organization and the Future of Life Institute. He had expected the recipients to cash out at most just over $20 million.

data.title: ECB President Lagarde Sees High Inflation Persisting in Near Future
data.description: European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde told the Yomiuri Shimbun that inflation is likely to remain high in the near future, according to Bloomberg. She said second-round effects so far are no worse than anticipated.

data.title: SEC Crypto Broker-Dealer Rule Proposal Submitted to White House for Review, Covers Four Securities Rules
data.description:
The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) submitted a proposal for crypto broker-dealer rules to the White House for regulatory review on November 3, 2026. According to Odaily, the proposal covers four provisions under the Securities Exchange Act: Rules 15c3-1, 15c3-3, 17a-3 and 17a-4. They concern net capital requirements, customer asset protection, recordkeeping and record retention. No draft or publication timeline has been made public.

An SEC staff statement issued in December 2025 provided guidance on some crypto asset custody arrangements but did not amend the rules or establish comprehensive custody standards.

Democrats won majorities in both chambers of Congress in the November 3, 2026, midterm elections and are expected to take control when the new Congress begins on January 3, 2027. Congressional Democrats could oversee the proposal through hearings, document requests and funding negotiations. Its adoption will depend on subsequent regulatory proceedings.

data.title: U.S. Stocks to Focus on Inflation Data and AI Infrastructure Earnings Next Week
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher citing Investor’s Business Daily, investors will focus on inflation data and a new round of corporate earnings next week amid market volatility following the U.S. midterm elections. So far, 88% of S&P 500 companies have reported results, with 84% exceeding consensus earnings-per-share estimates.

Cisco’s upcoming report will offer an indication of its progress toward its annual target of $7.5 billion in AI infrastructure orders. Investors will also watch CoreWeave’s data center buildout and order backlog. Emerging cloud providers such as CoreWeave have recently faced higher funding costs and pressure related to debt financing.

data.title: Cruises Attract More Gen Z and Millennial Travelers With Fares Near $30 a Day
data.description: Cruises are drawing more Gen Z and millennial travelers as higher airfare and hotel costs make all-inclusive vacations more appealing, Bloomberg News travel journalist Brittany Chang said, according to Bloomberg. Cruise lines are courting younger passengers with mega ships, entertainment, adult-only spaces and nostalgia, with some sailings costing as little as about $30 a day.

data.title: ECB President Christine Lagarde: No Guarantee of December Action, Developments Still Match Expectations
data.description: According to Jin10, ECB President Christine Lagarde said she could not guarantee the ECB would act in December, but developments remained in line with her expectations based on current information, barring a major change. Asked about criticism that the ECB had responded slowly to previous energy shocks through the Russia-Ukraine conflict, Lagarde said the issue was not unique to Europe but faced by everyone. She described the current environment as marked by major uncertainty and unpredictability, a breakdown of the familiar global order, trade and supply-chain disruptions, and excessive focus on security over efficiency, all of which were changing the operating environment for economic participants. She said the ECB had decided to set monetary policy based on data and one meeting at a time.

data.title: AI | Stricter Oversight Candidates Win Key Races After $110 Million Midterm Battle
data.description: Candidates favoring stricter artificial intelligence oversight won key congressional races after a $110 million midterm fight, aided by a pro-regulation political funding group backed in part by Anthropic PBC, Bloomberg reported. Americans are increasingly uneasy about the rapidly developing technology.

data.title: Ashley Koning: Affordability and Democracy Concerns Drove the Blue Wave
data.description: Rutgers University's Ashley Koning said affordability, concerns about democracy and government corruption helped drive voters toward Democrats in the Blue Wave, with significant shifts among Latino, young and independent voters, Bloomberg reported. She said Democrats face pressure to deliver tangible results on affordability before the 2028 election cycle.

data.title: Turkey Arrests Ex-Markets Regulator Deputy Chairman in Expanding Fund Probe
data.description: Turkish authorities arrested the former deputy chairman of the country’s markets regulator, state-run Anadolu Agency reported Saturday, according to Bloomberg. The arrest is the latest involving an executive in a widening fund scandal.

data.title: ECB President Christine Lagarde: No Signs of Second-Round Effects Beyond Forecasts
data.description: According to Jin10, ECB President Christine Lagarde said the ECB had not observed signs of second-round effects beyond its forecasts. It is closely monitoring forward-looking indicators, including multi-year wage agreements and companies’ wage expectations, but has not yet seen any signs of change. Lagarde said it was too early to prejudge whether forecasts would be raised, but noted that important changes had occurred since the ECB’s September forecasts. The energy futures curve had risen, which would affect both inflation and economic growth, although oil prices had recently fallen. Long-term interest rates had also risen. The ECB’s forecasts will determine how these factors affect medium-term inflation.

data.title: Bloomberg Strategist Mike McGlone Says Bitcoin Bear Market May Signal Further Losses for Stocks, Gold
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher, Bloomberg Intelligence senior commodities strategist Mike McGlone wrote that Bitcoin’s bear market could offer a signal for gold and other risk assets. He said U.S. President Donald Trump’s shift from opposing to supporting crypto helped him win reelection in 2024, but Bitcoin has now peaked and declined; historically, other risk assets could follow.

McGlone said Bitcoin’s 50-week moving average indicates a downtrend and that gold also faces downside risk. Gold’s volatility is currently about 2.2 times the S&P 500’s annualized volatility, its highest level since 2007, making it a highly volatile and highly correlated asset, he said. He added that Bitcoin’s bear market could signal a mean reversion in S&P 500 volatility toward its usual 1:1 relationship with gold. Risk assets face significant pullback risks, and the midterm elections could be a decisive factor, he said.

data.title: Josh Gottheimer Bought AI-Linked Stocks Despite Backing Congressional Trading Ban
data.description: According to CNBC, Rep. Josh Gottheimer, a Democrat helping shape his party’s artificial intelligence agenda, disclosed an Oct. 12 purchase of $1,001 to $15,000 in Benchmark Electronics stock and an Oct. 26 purchase of up to $15,000 in Applied Materials shares. His jointly owned Morgan Stanley account had also made three earlier purchases of Advanced Micro Devices stock. In July, Gottheimer was among 13 Democrats who voted for the Stop Insider Trading Act, which would bar lawmakers and their families from buying most individual stocks; the bill passed the House but has not become law. His spokesman said Gottheimer had given a third party full discretion over his investments and was awaiting congressional approval of a blind trust.
